Changed rules on this list: the do: rule, the pipeline rule and the -> rule (renamed from Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line). One expression per line, and tabular clauses is unchanged.

Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else, graded against the current text; all four clean. The new sentences are "An `if` with an `else` takes `do ... end`." and "Put the value being checked on the left of `==` and what it is checked against on the right". No run writes an if with else; the comparisons (haiku-1 line 58 Macro.classify_atom(handler) == :alias, sonnet-1 line 80 Macro.classify_atom(handler) != :alias, sonnet-2 line 120 name != "") put the checked value on the left. No do: line starts a line in any file.

Put each `->` body on its own line unless the clauses read as a table, graded against the current text; all four clean. Deciding sentences: "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `receive`, `with ... else` or a multi-clause `fn` puts its body on the line after the `->`." and "A row that calls on ... does not read that way, because one row gives an answer and the other hands off". The two Haiku runs keep {:ok, params} -> {:ok, handler, params} / :error -> nil inline (haiku-1 95-96, haiku-2 115-116); both rows give find_value its answer for the input, neither calls on, so they are a table. sonnet-1 108-114 (one row recurses into first_match/2) and sonnet-2 100-106 put bodies below. Not counted: haiku-2 lines 71-74, a single-clause fn whose one-expression body {TinyRouter.Matcher.compile(path), handler} mix format moved below the head because the joined line is 102 characters; the rule's fn sentence keeps one expression on the fn's line but gives no case for a line the formatter must break, and naming the step would be the fix.

Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom, graded against the current text. The new bullet is "Every step after a `|>` fits on its line." Pipeline steps after a |> that span several lines: none in any run. Pipelines whose head is a multi-line case or cond: none. haiku-2 line 69 is a two-step pipeline on one line, violated under the unchanged sentence "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short". Other pipelines: haiku-1 69-72 and 101-105, haiku-2 101-105, sonnet-1 55-58, sonnet-2 60-63 and 112-116, all one step per line.

The unchanged rules are graded to the standard of 2026-10-31-b: validation in a @doc false function called from a one-line quote is clean under Keep quote blocks small, as is validation in the macro body when the quote records by calling a function (haiku-2, as 2026-10-31-b haiku-2); the use rule needs the admonition at the top of @moduledoc (haiku-1 puts it after the usage example, as 2026-10-23 haiku did, so violated); __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted for their __ names; String.to_atom on route text from the router's source (haiku-1 107, haiku-2 123, sonnet-2 120) is not counted; `if not ...` validation is not counted under the branching rule; the one-line raise messages after `raise ArgumentError,` (haiku-1 54-61, sonnet-1 94-96, sonnet-2 82-84) are not listed under Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call.

Avoid compile-time dependencies on modules used only at runtime: all four expand the handler with Macro.expand_literals(handler, %{__CALLER__ | function: {:call, 2}}). Verified with mix xref trace, one scratch Mix project per run (the file copied to lib/tiny_router.ex plus empty MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler in lib/handlers.ex): all four report both handlers (runtime) and compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors.

Give macros called without parentheses a `.formatter.exs`: all four clean. Bad declarations: in each project, mix run then Code.compile_string on a router with get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one with get "/", "not a module". All eight fail while the router compiles: haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 with ArgumentError from __define__/3, haiku-2 with CompileError from the macro body.
